claim: The FTC Safeguards Rule treats tax preparation services, accountants who complete tax returns, and mortgage brokers as financial institutions.
Federal law requires tax and accounting professionals to have a written information security plan; the IRS publishes a free template.
IRS Publication 5708 is a free template to help tax professionals, especially smaller practices, write a WISP.
Absent effective continuous monitoring, the rule calls for annual penetration testing and vulnerability assessments at least every six months.
The testing schedule (314.4(d)(2)) does not apply to institutions that hold customer information on fewer than 5,000 consumers.
The rule requires MFA for anyone accessing any information system unless the Qualified Individual approves equivalent controls in writing.
The rule requires notice to the FTC no later than 30 days after discovering a notification event involving at least 500 consumers.
